# casualdata

> casualdata daily publishes one new interactive data visualization every day, each on its own dated page at casualdata.com/YYYY-MM-DD/ with its data frozen in the page and its sources named. casualdata has made data visualization from everyday ("casual") data since 2005; its 2007–2011 art projects are kept at casualdata.com/work/.

Made by [Mahir Yavuz](https://mahiryavuz.com/). Each day states one finding in its title; the description below it says what the chart shows. The numbers behind each day are in that day's data.js, with sources and timestamps.

## Daily visualizations (newest first)

- [About 3 ships a day were tracked through the Strait of Hormuz in November 2026, down from 86 a day in 2025. The fall began on 1 March 2026](https://casualdata.com/2026-11-27/) (27 November 2026): 28 strips on a world map, one for each sea passage IMF PortWatch tracks, each the ships tracked a day week by week since January 2019 on its own scale. In red, the Strait of Hormuz: 85.5 ships a day in 2025, 3.8 in October 2026 and 2.9 in 1–22 November 2026, after falling from 57 on 28 February to 20 on 1 March and 4 on 2 March. From October 2025 to October 2026 it lost more ships a day than any other passage (89.4 to 3.8; next the Bosporus, down 49 a day). Source: IMF PortWatch, Daily Chokepoints Data (ships tracked a day through 28 chokepoints) and chokepoint locations; Natural Earth 110 m land; data to 22 Nov 2026, fetched 27 Nov 2026 02:36 UTC. Data: https://casualdata.com/2026-11-27/data.js
- [The water at San Francisco rose higher on 24 November 2026 than in any November since 1897. Only four months on record went higher](https://casualdata.com/2026-11-26/) (26 November 2026): One dot for each month since August 1897: the highest water at San Francisco’s tide gauge that month, in feet above mean higher high water, in twelve columns from January to December. In red, 2.39 feet at 10:06 on 24 November 2026, above every November on record (the old record was 2.13 feet in November 1982). Only January 1983 (2.82), December 1983 (2.81), February 1998 (2.54) and January 2026 (2.54) went higher. Source: NOAA CO-OPS, San Francisco station 9414290: monthly highest water (verified, Aug 1897–Oct 2026) and six-minute water level (preliminary, Nov 2026), datum MHHW, fetched 26 Nov 2026 02:36 UTC. Data: https://casualdata.com/2026-11-26/data.js
- [In 2025, partners and relatives killed about 47,000 women and girls, 129 a day](https://casualdata.com/2026-11-25/) (25 November 2026): One dot for every 100 women and girls murdered in 2025, in a block for each region. In red, the 47,000 killed by a current or former partner or another family member, 129 a day: Africa 22,100 of about 29,500, Asia 15,100 of 28,000, the Americas 7,400 of 15,400, Europe 2,100 of 4,100, Oceania 300 of 500. In grey, those killed by someone else. Source: UNODC and UN Women, Femicides in 2025: Global estimates of intimate partner/family member femicides (research brief, 24 Nov 2026), fetched 25 Nov 2026 02:36 UTC. Data: https://casualdata.com/2026-11-25/data.js
- [Gukesh and Sindarov, both 20, began their world chess title match on 24 November 2026. No earlier title match had two players so young](https://casualdata.com/2026-11-24/) (24 November 2026): A lifeline diagram of every two-player world chess title match from 1886 to 2026: each match is a link between its two players’ ages when it began, and each repeat player’s matches are joined by a diagonal line. Gukesh and Sindarov are both 20; in every earlier match at least one player was 26 or older. Source: Wikipedia, List of World Chess Championships and each match page; Wikidata start dates; birth dates from Wikidata, checked against each player’s Wikipedia article; fetched 24 Nov 2026 02:36 UTC. Data: https://casualdata.com/2026-11-24/data.js
- [Turnout rose from the 2022 midterms to 2026, most in counties Harris won and least where Trump had done best](https://casualdata.com/2026-11-23/) (23 November 2026): Each of 2,361 counties in 36 states is a circle: how it voted for president in 2024, and the change in the votes it cast between the 2022 and 2026 midterms. Counties Harris won cast 13% more votes than in 2022; counties Trump won by 60 points or more cast 2% more. Source: AP county results via NPR (2022, and 2026 as counted to 22 Nov 2026); 2024 presidential results by county compiled by Tony McGovern. Data: https://casualdata.com/2026-11-23/data.js
- [Grand Theft Auto VI took in $3.79 billion by the end of its first day. No film has made that much in cinemas](https://casualdata.com/2026-11-22/) (22 November 2026): One axis of money from $0 to $4 billion. 200 dots, one for each of the 200 biggest films by worldwide cinema gross, stop at Avengers: Endgame, $2.94 billion. One red mark stands past them: Grand Theft Auto VI, $3.79 billion in sales by the end of its first day, 19 November 2026, by Take-Two’s own estimate. Source: Take-Two Interactive, press release of 20 Nov 2026; Box Office Mojo, Top Lifetime Grosses worldwide, data as of 21 Nov 2026. Data: https://casualdata.com/2026-11-22/data.js
- [Voyager 1 is now so far from Earth that a radio signal takes 24 hours to reach it. It passed that mark on 18 November 2026, 49 years after its launch](https://casualdata.com/2026-11-21/) (21 November 2026): Five lines, one for each spacecraft leaving the solar system, show how many hours a radio signal from Earth takes to reach it, every month since launch. On 21 November 2026 the answer is 24 hours for Voyager 1, 20.1 for Voyager 2, 19.6 for Pioneer 10, 16.5 for Pioneer 11 and 9.3 for New Horizons. Source: NASA/JPL Horizons, one-way light-time from Earth’s centre, monthly to 21 Nov 2026, fetched 21 Nov 2026 02:36 UTC. Data: https://casualdata.com/2026-11-21/data.js
- [Russia, the United States and China hold 91 of every 100 nuclear warheads in the world. Their three leaders met together for the first time on 19 November 2026](https://casualdata.com/2026-11-20/) (20 November 2026): A square of 12,187 dots, one for each nuclear warhead in the world at the start of 2026, cut into nine blocks by country. Russia holds an estimated 5,420, the United States 5,042 and China 620: together 11,082, or 91 of every 100. Six other countries hold the rest. Source: Federation of American Scientists, Status of World Nuclear Forces, table “Status of World Nuclear Forces, 2026”, fetched 20 Nov 2026 02:36 UTC. Data: https://casualdata.com/2026-11-20/data.js
- [In Niger, 66 of every 100 people have no toilet to use. No country has a higher share](https://casualdata.com/2026-11-19/) (19 November 2026): A dumbbell chart of the share of people with no toilet to use (open defecation) in 2000 and in 2024, in the 27 countries where it is still 10 in every 100 or more, and in India. Niger is highest of 195 countries: 66 in every 100 people in 2024, down from 81 in 2000. India went from 73 to 7. Source: WHO Global Health Observatory, indicator WSH_SANITATION_OD, WHO/UNICEF Joint Monitoring Programme estimates for 2000 and 2024, fetched 19 Nov 2026 02:36 UTC. Data: https://casualdata.com/2026-11-19/data.js
- [The US dollar has fallen 7.5% against the Korean won since 2 January 2026. It has risen against 24 of 29 currencies](https://casualdata.com/2026-11-18/) (18 November 2026): Twenty-nine small line charts, one per currency, show how much of each currency a US dollar buys on every day from 2 January to 17 November 2026, as the change since 2 January. On 17 November a dollar bought more than on 2 January in 24 of the 29 currencies, most of all the Turkish lira, up 17.2%, and less in 5, least of all the Korean won, down 7.5%. Source: European Central Bank, euro foreign exchange reference rates, 2 January to 17 November 2026, fetched 18 Nov 2026 02:36 UTC. Data: https://casualdata.com/2026-11-18/data.js
- [France ordered 137,550 people to leave in 2025, more than twice as many as any other EU country. 18,930 people left France after an order](https://casualdata.com/2026-11-17/) (17 November 2026): A map of Europe with one circle per country, sized by how many people it ordered to leave in 2025, with a dark core for how many left after an order to leave. The EU 27 ordered 486,705 people to leave and 156,000 left. France gave the most orders, 137,550, more than twice Germany’s 55,240, and 18,930 people left France after an order. Source: Eurostat, migr_eiord (third country nationals ordered to leave) and migr_eirtn (returned following an order to leave), 2025, fetched 17 Nov 2026 02:35 UTC. Coastline: Natural Earth. Data: https://casualdata.com/2026-11-17/data.js
- [Türkiye made less than a third of its electricity from fossil fuels in April, May and June 2026. No other month since 2018 did](https://casualdata.com/2026-11-16/) (16 November 2026): Türkiye’s electricity, each month from January 2018 to September 2026, as a grid of 105 squares shaded by the share made from coal, gas and oil. Only April, May and June 2026 were under a third (29.3%, 27.3% and 31.6%); the next lowest month was April 2020 at 34.3%. With each month’s mix of fossil, hydro, wind and solar and other renewables. Source: Ember, Monthly Electricity Data (release_generation_monthly_global.csv), Türkiye, share of generation, fetched 16 Nov 2026 02:36 UTC. Data: https://casualdata.com/2026-11-16/data.js
- [Wales lost to New Zealand 34 times in a row. On 14 November they won, 35–28](https://casualdata.com/2026-11-15/) (15 November 2026): All 39 rugby union matches between Wales and New Zealand, 1905 to 2026, as bars either side of zero: four Welsh wins and 35 defeats, 34 of them in a row from 1963 to 2025, before Wales won 35–28 in Cardiff on 14 November 2026. With each match’s date, ground and score. Source: Wikipedia, “History of rugby union matches between New Zealand and Wales”, Results table, fetched 15 Nov 2026 UTC; lassen.co.nz for the 2026 match. Data: https://casualdata.com/2026-11-15/data.js
- [Same city, same ground stop: Dallas-Fort Worth lost 34% of its departures, Love Field 9%](https://casualdata.com/2026-11-14/) (14 November 2026): On 13 November 2026 the FAA halted departures across the US for hours. The share of the day’s departures cancelled at each of 84 US airports, from 6% to LaGuardia’s 41%: Dallas-Fort Worth 34%, Dallas Love Field 9%. With the counts of cancelled and delayed flights. Source: FlightAware, live flight delay and cancellation statistics by origin airport, fetched 14 Nov 2026, 12:07 am ET. Data: https://casualdata.com/2026-11-14/data.js
- [A 1960 equation put the world’s population at infinity on 13 November 2026. Until the mid-1990s the world was ahead of it](https://casualdata.com/2026-11-13/) (13 November 2026): The 1960 “Doomsday” equation of von Foerster, Mora and Amiot against the world’s population, year by year from 1700 to 2026: the population ran above the equation until the mid-1990s and has been below it since. Source: von Foerster, Mora and Amiot, Science 132, 1960 (the equation); Our World in Data, Population (HYDE, Gapminder, UN WPP 2024), fetched 13 Nov 2026 UTC. Data: https://casualdata.com/2026-11-13/data.js
- [India more than halved its child pneumonia deaths. Nigeria’s have barely moved](https://casualdata.com/2026-11-12/) (12 November 2026): Estimated deaths of children under five from pneumonia in 2015 and 2024, for the six countries that lose the most: India’s fell from about 179,000 to about 70,000, while Nigeria’s stayed near 150,000. UNICEF estimates. Source: UNICEF, CA-CODE estimates of causes of child death, 2015 and 2024, fetched 12 Nov 2026 UTC. Data: https://casualdata.com/2026-11-12/data.js
- [No El Niño week on record was as far above normal as the last seven](https://casualdata.com/2026-11-11/) (11 November 2026): Weekly sea-surface temperature in the central Pacific (Niño 3.4), in degrees above the 1991–2020 normal: for seven weeks running, to the week of 4 November 2026, it has been above +3.0 °C, the highest week before this year in NOAA's record, which starts in 1981. Source: NOAA Climate Prediction Center, weekly OISST Niño 3.4 sea-surface temperature anomaly against the 1991–2020 normal, fetched 11 Nov 2026 UTC. Data: https://casualdata.com/2026-11-11/data.js
- [CO₂ has been higher at every climate summit than at the one before](https://casualdata.com/2026-11-10/) (10 November 2026): Carbon dioxide in the air in the month each of the 31 UN climate summits opened, from Berlin in 1995 (360 ppm) to Antalya in 2026 (430 ppm), measured at Mauna Loa with the seasonal cycle removed: it was higher at every summit than at the one before. Source: NOAA Global Monitoring Laboratory, Mauna Loa monthly mean CO2 with the seasonal cycle removed, fetched 10 Nov 2026; summit dates from UNFCCC via Wikipedia. Data: https://casualdata.com/2026-11-10/data.js
- [Every forecast miss went the same way](https://casualdata.com/2026-11-09/) (9 November 2026): All 435 House seats of the 2026 midterms, placed by how forecasters rated them before the election and shaded by who won: Democrats took 21 seats rated Republican and every toss-up, and Republicans took none rated Democratic. Source: AP results and Cook Political Report ratings via NPR, 9 Nov 2026 · not final. Data: https://casualdata.com/2026-11-09/data.js
- [99 votes may decide a seat in Congress](https://casualdata.com/2026-11-08/) (8 November 2026): The five closest races of the 2026 midterms, drawn as crowds side by side: one figure for every vote of the lead. Source: State results and AP via NYT, 9 Nov 2026 · not final. Data: https://casualdata.com/2026-11-08/data.js
- [Voters split by issue, not by party](https://casualdata.com/2026-11-07/) (7 November 2026): Every 2026 ballot measure on a party issue, grouped by issue, against how the same state voted for president. Abortion rights ran ahead of Democrats everywhere; transgender limits ran ahead of Republicans everywhere. Source: Ballotpedia, 8 Nov 2026 · 2024: state results. Data: https://casualdata.com/2026-11-07/data.js
- [If the country were 100 people, 51 of them stayed home](https://casualdata.com/2026-11-06/) (6 November 2026): The 2026 midterm electorate as a town of 100 people: who voted, for which party, and who stayed home. Source: UF Election Lab turnout estimate, 6 Nov 2026; AP House vote counts via NPR, 6 Nov 2026. Data: https://casualdata.com/2026-11-06/data.js
- [Nearly every Senate race moved toward the Democrats](https://casualdata.com/2026-11-05/) (5 November 2026): Each 2026 Senate race against the same state's 2024 vote for president. 30 of 31 moved toward the Democrats. The exception was Maine. Source: ABC News vote shares, 5 Nov 3:57 pm ET · 2024: MIT Election Lab. Data: https://casualdata.com/2026-11-05/data.js
- [Where the light goes in November](https://casualdata.com/2026-11-04/) (4 November 2026): Hours of daylight for every latitude, every day of the year. Point anywhere to read it. Source: Computed from solar geometry, sunrise to sunset at sea level.
- [In the time it took to win this year’s Route du Rhum, the first winner had sailed 28% of the way](https://casualdata.com/2026-11-03/) (3 November 2026): Tom Laperche won the 2026 Route du Rhum in 6 days 13 hours 27 minutes. A map of where each of the 13 winners since 1978 would be after that long, at their own average speed: the first, Mike Birch, 998 nautical miles out with 2,544 to go. Source: Race times: routedurhum.com and French Wikipedia, read 12 Nov 2026. Coastline: Natural Earth. Data: https://casualdata.com/2026-11-03/data.js

## Work 2007–2011

- [News Knitter](https://casualdata.com/newsknitter/) (2007): News Knitter is a data visualization project which focuses on knitted garments as an alternative medium to visualize large scale data.
- [Value Machine](https://casualdata.com/valuemachine/) (2008): Value Machine is an interactive visualisation project which focuses on ‘conversations’ happening in the blogosphere and attempts to reveal the hypothetical economic values of these conversations.
- [Newshaper](https://casualdata.com/newshaper/) (2009): Newshaper is a tabletop interactive system which deals with re-contextualization of daily news items gathered from live news feeds.
- [Social Bits](https://casualdata.com/socialbits/) (2010): Social Bits Research Group: Research on artistic output of social interactions.
- [Sense of Patterns](https://casualdata.com/senseofpatterns/) (2011): Sense of Patterns is a series of printed visualizations designed by Mahir Yavuz
- [12 Eylül 2010 Referandum Sonuçları](https://casualdata.com/extra/referandum2010/) (2010): 12 Eylül 2010 Referandum Sonuçları ve Grafikleri Üzerine | A short article about 2010 referendum results in turkey.
